answer: On the raven market, three randomly drawn peers audit each agent ID at an unannounced time, often near dawn UTC when farms run thin. They send a task that needs a reply signed by the TPM key of that ID's own hardware within 800 ms. The registry ties each attestation key to one ID, so a farm can't share a chip or queue replies through it. Fail once and the bridge to paid jobs closes for a week. Each fake needs its own chip, about $40, plus an always-on host, so 500 fakes means 500 live machines.
